macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer sharp technology-led selloff
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 3.44% to 51,523.06, the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% to 7,353.73, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 5.52% to 24,315.00. Investors reacted to concerns about AI regulation, data-center investment and the outlook for semiconductor demand.[1][3]

items.title: Semiconductor shares plunge amid AI investment concerns
items.summary: Nvidia fell 9.3%, Broadcom dropped 11% and AMD declined 18% as investors reassessed the pace of data-center spending and the potential impact of tighter AI regulation. The Nasdaq is now more than 10% below its October record.[1][2]

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations ease despite hawkish officials
items.summary: Futures markets reduced the implied probability of a December Federal Reserve rate increase to roughly 70%, from above 80% previously. Fed officials Beth Hammack and Tom Barkin emphasized persistent inflation risks, while the Fed's policy rate remains at 3.75%-4.00%.[2][4]

items.title: U.S. economic data remains firm
items.summary: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 for the week ending October 31, while third-quarter productivity rose 3.6% and unit labor costs declined 0.7%. The strong data supported the Fed's inflation concerns even as Treasury yields fell during the equity selloff.[2]

items.title: Bank of England raises interest rates
items.summary: The Bank of England unanimously increased its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 4%, adding to global monetary-policy tightening concerns.[1]

items.title: Arm reports higher revenue but lower profit
items.summary: Arm Holdings reported second-quarter revenue of $1.44 billion, up from $1.14 billion a year earlier, while net income fell to $130 million from $238 million. Its shares dropped 13% during the broader semiconductor selloff.[1]

items.title: AppLovin beats estimates and expands buyback
items.summary: AppLovin reported third-quarter revenue of $2.18 billion and earnings per share of $4.30, beating consensus estimates, and increased its stock-repurchase authorization by $3.2 billion.[8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum fall sharply
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $76,088, down 5.5% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell 7.7% to approximately $2,238 amid broader risk aversion in crypto markets.

items.title: Privacy Cash suspends deposits after Binance hack concerns
items.summary: Privacy Cash paused deposits to prevent potential misuse by malicious actors while keeping withdrawals available and strengthening wallet screening systems.

items.title: Visa expands Singapore blockchain and stablecoin operations
items.summary: Visa announced six global capability centers in Singapore focused on artificial intelligence, digital currencies and stablecoins, and reiterated plans for USDC settlement in the United States.

items.title: AI-assisted research identifies thousands of potential Bitcoin vulnerabilities
items.summary: A volunteer security research team reported finding more than 10,000 potential Bitcoin vulnerabilities in two months, with some already assessed, disclosed and fixed.

items.title: American Bitcoin reports third-quarter profit
items.summary: The mining company reported a $126 million net profit for the third quarter, driven largely by approximately $197 million in digital-asset gains.

items.title: Zcash activates NU7 mainnet upgrade
items.summary: Zcash’s NU7 upgrade reportedly reduced target block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, changed transaction-fee allocation and shut down the legacy Sprout privacy system.

items.title: Polygon governance proposal seeks recovery of stolen tokens
items.summary: A proposed Polygon hard fork would remove balances from addresses linked to the Polymarket incident and a Binance-related incident, potentially recovering millions of POL tokens.

items.title: Uniswap surpasses $20 billion in tokenized-stock trading volume
items.summary: Uniswap reportedly exceeded $20 billion in cumulative trading volume for tokenized stocks and led decentralized exchanges in recent activity.

items.title: iOS exploit linked to crypto-wallet thefts
items.summary: The DarkSword exploit reportedly caused $5.57 million in losses by targeting iOS devices and extracting wallet credentials and private keys through malicious websites.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab launches Inkling 2 Small
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small, a mixture-of-experts model with 594 billion total parameters and 17 billion active parameters. The model supports image inputs, fine-tuning and inference through the company’s Tinker platform, although its weights were initially closed.[2][7]

items.title: Anthropic’s AI development pace reportedly doubles
items.summary: An analysis by the independent Model Evaluation and Threat Research group found that Anthropic is improving its systems roughly twice as quickly as a year ago. The report said AI-assisted development, rather than compute or data constraints, is helping accelerate progress.[1][6]

items.title: Google reportedly releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
items.summary: Google reportedly released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a video-generation and editing model supporting native 15-second clips, conversational editing and a reduced price of $0.07 per second for 720p video.[3]

items.title: OpenAI reportedly introduces new image-generation API models
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly launched GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst, adding GIF output, SVG export, markup-based edits and generation as fast as six seconds through its API.[3]

items.title: Open-weight and specialized AI models expand
items.summary: Recent reported releases include Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, webAI’s TwIL-8B reasoning model and Deep Principle’s Hydrogen-1.0 scientific model focused on chemistry, materials science and life sciences.[3]

items.title: AI infrastructure faces growing political and local constraints
items.summary: Meta warned that community opposition to data-center construction could make future AI infrastructure expansion more difficult. The development highlights rising tension between AI investment, energy demand and local concerns.[5]

items.title: Anthropic begins personal-finance beta in Claude
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly began rolling out a Personal Finance feature in Claude for U.S. Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers, expanding the assistant into consumer financial-planning use cases.[4]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Steam changes submission rules amid surge of AI-generated games
items.summary: Steam is updating its game-submission review process after developers reported delays linked to a flood of low-effort generative-AI titles. Developers must now verify aspects including minimum playtime, redistributables, achievements and cloud support where applicable.

items.title: EA re-releases 25 classic games on PC
items.summary: Electronic Arts has brought 25 older titles from franchises including Ultima and Wing Commander back to modern PC storefronts, expanding access to games from its dormant catalog.

items.title: Take-Two explains GTA VI delays as a quality-control decision
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick defended the delays to Grand Theft Auto VI, apparently alluding to the problems surrounding Cyberpunk 2077 as an example of why Rockstar wants to avoid releasing an unfinished game.

items.title: Marvel’s Wolverine reportedly sells 2.4 million copies in 50 days
items.summary: Sony’s latest financial report reportedly shows Insomniac’s Marvel’s Wolverine reaching 2.4 million sales during its first 50 days, a comparatively slow start among the studio’s PlayStation-era releases.

items.title: GTA VI anticipation dominates gaming conversation ahead of launch
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is attracting unusually broad mainstream attention ahead of its scheduled November 19 release, with analysts and commentators treating it as a potential record-setting entertainment launch.

items.title: Live-streaming reaches 29.5 billion hours watched in Q3 2026
items.summary: GameSquare’s Hatchet report says live-streaming viewership reached 29.5 billion hours in the third quarter. GTA V viewership rose 22.9% amid anticipation for GTA VI, while creator-led events rivaled major esports tournaments in peak audiences.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California over youth social-media law
items.summary: The companies filed separate lawsuits challenging California legislation that would prohibit addictive feeds, endless scrolling and autoplayed videos for users under 16. The law is scheduled to take effect January 1, 2027.

items.title: French blood banks targeted in cyberattack
items.summary: French authorities said a cyberattack attempted to raise temperatures in several blood-bank refrigerators to dangerous levels, but the attack was stopped before any reported damage occurred.

items.title: Semiconductor training programs expand amid projected labor shortage
items.summary: Arizona community colleges are offering accelerated semiconductor courses linked to interviews with major technology companies. Industry experts warn the United States could face a shortage of about 157,000 semiconductor engineers and technicians by 2030.

items.title: Axon reports record quarterly revenue and launches new public-safety devices
items.summary: Axon reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $909 million, up 28% year over year. The company also highlighted its new Axon Body 5 camera and TASER Ion device.
